thesis: Held. Linde's Oct 29 Q3 2026 report showed record sales of ~$9.4B (+9%) with higher full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance, and on Nov 19 Kepler Cheuvreux upgraded the stock to Buy citing an expected 2027 margin recovery. This suggests the industrial-gas pricing/productivity model still supports holding after a +11.9% 60-day move, with the stock ~6.9% below its 52-week high. The counter-case is that reported EPS was weighed by a restructuring charge, Q4 guidance assumes no economic improvement, and several insiders (including the CFO) sold shares in early November; the upgrade is analyst opinion rather than a new company disclosure, so multiple factors contribute without one decisive new catalyst. No litigation with a scheduled near-term step, and no restatement/auditor/indictment history, surfaced in this run's searches.
invalidation: Q4 adjusted EPS below guidance or another guidance cut; additional restructuring charges signaling broader operating weakness

thesis: Southern Company's Nov 5 Q3 2026 report showed adjusted EPS of $1.94 (vs $1.60), raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $4.70, and said it may raise 2027+ ranges in February; data center usage rose 59% in the quarter, with 21 GW of contracted large-load customers plus ~7 GW in late-stage talks. This suggests a credible, company-specific growth catalyst behind the +10.5% 60-day move, with shares ~6.3% below the 52-week high and just above the 200-day average. Counter-case: political rhetoric about pausing new Georgia data center developments could cap future load growth, and Treasury yields near 5% pressure utility valuations. Management cites signed contracts, but the long-term guidance raise is still pending. No scheduled litigation step found; Georgia Power base rates are frozen through 2028.
invalidation: Regulatory or legislative action in Georgia restricting new data center interconnections, or the February guidance update failing to lift long-term ranges

thesis: Home Depot reported Q3 fiscal 2026 on Nov 17: sales $43.4B (+4.9%), comparable sales +2.2% (above a ~1.8% StreetAccount estimate), online comps ~+13%, and adjusted EPS $3.86 vs $3.74. This suggests the home-improvement demand trough is easing and explains much of the +13.6% 60-day move. However, it lowered its full-year comp outlook to ~1.4% (from flat to +2%) and narrowed adjusted EPS growth to ~2%, and comparable transactions still fell 0.5%. Positive but not decisive. CFO Richard McPhail becomes CEO Nov 23 while Ted Decker stays chair after a medical leave; the board describes this as planned succession, not execution-driven, so it is not flagged as leadership_turnover. No scheduled litigation or governance history surfaced.
invalidation: Q4 comps turning negative or another cut to FY26 EPS guidance

thesis: Held. Costco's company-reported October 2026 sales (four weeks ended Nov 1) rose 12.6% to $24.50B, with total comparable sales +11.1% (+7.3% excluding gasoline and FX) and digitally-enabled sales +22.5%; the nine-week figure was +12.8%. That confirmed, company-disclosed demand trend sits behind the +22.1% 60-day move and the stock trading ~2.7% below its Nov 17 52-week high, which suggests holding remains supported. The strongest counter-case is valuation (P/E ~53) plus a consumer class action (Stockov v. Costco, N.D. Ill.) over pass-through of tariff refunds; even with that premium, a 7.3% underlying comp and accelerating digital growth are fundamental rather than multiple-driven, and the class action has no scheduled ruling or trial date surfaced in this run. No restatement, auditor or indictment history found.
invalidation: Monthly comparable sales ex-gas/FX decelerating below ~5%, or a Q1 FY27 report showing membership fee income or renewal-rate deterioration

thesis: P&G is +16.6% over 60 days and ~3.3% below its Nov 17 52-week high. Its Oct 22 fiscal Q1 2027 release showed net and organic sales both +4%, with volume +2.4 points carrying most of the growth, and it maintained 1%-3% full-year organic growth guidance while lifting all-in sales guidance for the Thorne acquisition. This suggests volume-led, company-specific momentum. Against that, management flagged a $1.4B after-tax commodity and freight headwind for FY27 and only maintained (not raised) organic guidance, and part of the recent move likely reflects defensive rotation during a broad market selloff. Multiple contributing factors, none clearly dominant. No scheduled litigation step or governance history surfaced.
invalidation: Fiscal Q2 organic growth falling below the 1%-3% guide range or a guidance cut driven by commodity costs

thesis: Held. Lilly's Oct 29 Q3 2026 8-K showed revenue of $24.4B (+39%) driven by Mounjaro and Zepbound, and full-year revenue guidance was raised to $91.0-$92.0B (its third raise this year); on Nov 12 China's regulator approved oral orforglipron, already sold in the U.S. as Foundayo. These confirmed, company-specific events suggest the incretin franchise still supports holding after a +18.7% 60-day move. The strongest counter-case is that the EPS guide was held at $35-$36 because of $4.57/share of acquired IPR&D charges, and the stock fell ~2.3% today to ~8.4% below its Nov 16 high; those are one-off business-development charges rather than operating deterioration, and the underlying EPS guide was raised, so the read holds. No litigation with a scheduled near-term step or governance history surfaced.
invalidation: A guidance cut or a sharp sequential slowdown in Mounjaro/Zepbound revenue; a safety issue or pricing action materially affecting the GLP-1 franchise

thesis: Held. Visa fell ~3.1% today to $402.54 (~9% below its Nov 5 52-week high), with coverage tying it to an extortion group's claim of stolen data from a third-party vendor; Visa says the incident originated at an Asia-Pacific service provider, its own systems were not impacted, and there is no indication card numbers were affected. The stock is still +12.2% over 60 days, but this run found no new company-disclosed fundamental catalyst for November, and the drop reads as sentiment-driven rather than a disclosed deterioration. The DOJ debit-monopolization case has discovery extended to Jan 29, 2027 with trial not expected before 2028, so it does not meet the scheduled-step-within-90-days bar. Holding still looks supported, but the evidence is mixed rather than a clear net positive.
invalidation: Confirmation that Visa cardholder or payment data was compromised, or adverse developments (e.g. settlement terms) in the DOJ debit case that impair the fee model

thesis: SK hynix ADRs are down ~35% over 60 days and sit ~1.5% above their 52-week low. The drop is part of a broad memory/semiconductor selloff (sharp drops after Oct 29 Q3 results, a ~13% one-day fall alongside Micron and Samsung) amid valuation worries and CXMT competition, even though Q3 operating margin was ~80% and Counterpoint says memory prices were still rising. This is a sector-wide move rather than a company-specific deterioration. Pending litigation includes ITC patent investigations (target completion Aug 30, 2027) and a June 2026 DRAM indirect-purchaser antitrust class action with no scheduled ruling surfaced. The 200-day trend check could not run (only 93 real bars since the July 2026 ADR listing). Falling-knife conditions with no stabilizing catalyst don't support a new entry.
invalidation: Price stabilization with Q4 results (expected late January) confirming contracted 2027-28 HBM capacity and margins

thesis: Held. Apple's fiscal Q4 report beat estimates alongside a planned leadership transition (John Ternus CEO, Tim Cook executive chairman), and the stock trades ~3.2% below its Nov 13 52-week high, about 15% above its 200-day average, which suggests holding is still supported. Counter-evidence: former chairman Arthur Levinson filed to sell ~90,000 shares (~$32M) near the highs, and Apple's Epic contempt appeal is pending at the Supreme Court (Epic filed its brief in November) with no decision yet; the DOJ antitrust case has no trial date and has seen settlement talks. The insider sale is a single, pre-filed disposition rather than a disclosed fundamental change, but no single dominant new catalyst resolves the picture either. No restatement/auditor/indictment history surfaced.
invalidation: A Supreme Court ruling or DOJ settlement that materially restricts App Store economics, or guidance pointing to iPhone/Services deceleration

thesis: AMD fell ~7.7% today (as much as ~10% intraday) on 2.0x volume after Hunterbrook, the media arm of a fund that disclosed a short position, alleged that blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT kept receiving newer AMD firmware and flagged China/HK exposure (~22% of FY25 revenue). Hunterbrook itself says its findings do not establish that AMD sold chips to blacklisted firms, and Reuters and CNBC could not verify the central claim. AMD says the claims misrepresent its business and that it complies with export law. The stock is -13.9% over 60 days but still above its 200-day average; part of today's drop is also tied to retail rotation into the Anthropic IPO and yields near 5%. With an unverified short report and no regulatory action yet, the picture is unresolved and largely sentiment-driven, so it doesn't support a new entry this cycle.
invalidation: A clear rebuttal or regulator statement clearing AMD of export-control exposure, combined with stabilizing AI-semiconductor sentiment

thesis: Manulife traded ~8.6x its 30-day average volume today while slipping ~1.8% and crossing below its 50-day average, but this run found no company announcement behind the spike; Nov 20 is its ex-dividend date, so the volume may partly be mechanical (dividend-related or index/flow trading) rather than fundamental. Its Nov 4 Q3 2026 report was mixed: core earnings C$2.1B (+4% constant currency) and core EPS +6%, with Asia core earnings +17%, but net income fell ~21% on a C$701M charge from public-equity returns and hedge ineffectiveness. With no identified catalyst for today's move and mixed recent results, there is no clear setup for a new entry.
invalidation: An identified company-specific catalyst (e.g. capital return or a strategic transaction) explaining the volume, plus a return above the 50-day average

thesis: Insmed jumped ~20% today on 4.0x volume after Bloomberg reported that Sanofi is working with advisers on a potential takeover. Neither company has confirmed talks, there is no agreement, and any deal could be weeks away or not happen. Q3 revenue of $524.4M (BRINSUPRI and ARIKAYCE) is a real fundamental base, and the stock is now ~18% above its 200-day average. But today's move is an unconfirmed M&A report, not a company-disclosed event; entering now would mostly be a bet on a deal that could collapse and reverse the gain. No patent trial or governance history surfaced in this run.
invalidation: A signed, announced acquisition agreement (removes deal uncertainty) or company confirmation of talks with defined terms
